title: Subeg Singh Reads the Boy’s Forehead and Challenges the Nawab

blocks.text: Refusing to accept appearances, Subeg Singh asks to see the boy closely so he can understand what has happened under torture and pressure. The request gives the scene a sudden intimacy, shifting attention from the court's spectacle to the father's searching discernment.

When he studies the child, Subeg Singh asks to see the boy closely in a spiritual as well as physical sense, interpreting the moment through destiny, inscription, and the Guru's Name. He symbolically wipes away the fate he reads on the boy's forehead while uttering Akal and Satnam, turning the body itself into a site of contest between imposed identity and recovered truth.

The nawab, unsettled by that act, immediately tests whether the child will still repeat the kalma or return to Sikh speech. What follows becomes another trial of language, memory, and spiritual allegiance.
